# Release Notes - awake 0.8.0-beta-pre1.0.0

> [!WARNING]
> **This is a PRE-RELEASE of the upcoming 1.0.0 stable version and has NOT
> been fully tested yet.** It ships the complete 1.0 feature set ahead of
> the stabilization round; the long-run soak verification is still in
> progress and the 1.0.0 stable tag will follow once it passes. Use it to
> try the new features early - stick to 0.7.0-beta if you need a
> battle-tested build.

Release date: 2026-10-24
Package: `awake-daemon.win64.zip`

The eighth beta release of **awake**, a Windows command line tool that keeps
the system awake - and the first pre-release on the road to **1.0.0**. It
completes the planned 1.0 feature set: script-friendly output, detailed
status information, daemon logging, power event awareness and the release
hardening verification tooling.

## Highlights

- **Timed keep-awake polish**: keep-awake and screen keep-awake now report
  their remaining time in `awake status` (`expires in ...`).
- **Script-friendly output** (`awake list`, `--json`, `--no-color` /
  `NO_COLOR`): plain text and JSON modes for scripts and CI. `awake status`
  prints a full JSON object with every state field.
- **Status details**: `awake status` shows the active power plan sleep and
  hibernate timeouts, the screensaver setting and which execution state
  requests the daemon currently holds (`Requests: system / system + display`).
- **Daemon logging** (`awake log`): rolling log files
  (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\awake\logs\daemon\daemon-YYYYMMDD.log`, appended across
  restarts of the same day) with a configurable level and size/file-count
  limits, hot-applied via RELOAD. `awake log export [path]` packs the log
  files into a dependency-free .zip for issue attachments. Logging is
  **enabled by default**.
- **Power event awareness**: the daemon watches for resume-from-sleep events
  and immediately re-applies the execution state; `awake status` shows how
  long ago the last resume was handled.
- **Hardened pipe server**: oversized or malformed requests are dropped
  safely, remote connections are rejected and the pipe name cannot be
  hijacked (`FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE`).
- **Elevation guard (option A)**: the daemon refuses to run elevated - a
  high-integrity pipe cannot be controlled from a normal shell, which left
  users with an uncontrollable daemon. `daemon on` in an elevated shell
  fails with a clear error. Automation environments can opt out with
  `AWAKE_ALLOW_ELEVATED=1`.
- **Performance**: the parsed watch list is cached by file stat, the process
  scan stops as soon as every watched name is found, and a vanished
  `awake.ini` is recreated automatically.

## R16 verification tooling

The release hardening pass (R16) ships its tooling with this release:

- `utils/test/acceptance.py` - three-tier acceptance orchestrator producing
  `build/verification/report.md` and `results.json`.
- `utils/test/stress.py` - concurrency storm and randomized pipe fuzzing.
- `utils/test/soak.py` - long-run stability verification (F1 expiry
  precision, watch churn, memory trend).
- `utils/test/manual-checklist.md` - the formal manual review checklist.

The long-run soak for 1.0.0 is still in progress; this pre-release ships
without it (see the warning above).

## Full command list

```
awake help               Show the help message.
awake version            Show the version.
awake aliases            Show every command alias.
awake 0                  Disable keep-awake.
awake 1                  Enable keep-awake (blocks idle sleep/hibernation).
awake 1 for <period>     Enable keep-awake for a limited time.
awake 1 until <HH:MM>    Enable keep-awake until that clock time.
awake status             Show daemon, keep-awake, screen, autostart and
                         watch list status.
awake list               List the watched applications (--json for JSON).
awake screen on          Keep the screen on (blocks screen off, screensaver
                         and idle lock).
awake screen on for <period>   Keep the screen on for a limited time.
awake screen off         Stop keeping the screen on.
awake daemon on          Start the background daemon.
awake daemon off         Stop the background daemon.
awake daemon enable      Start the daemon automatically at logon.
awake daemon disable     Do not start the daemon automatically at logon.
awake log                Show or change daemon logging (on / off / level /
                         max-files / max-size / export [path]).
awake reload             Re-read the configuration file immediately.
awake reset              Reset the configuration file (asks for
                         confirmation).
awake add <imagename>    Add an image name to the watch list.
awake del <imagename>    Remove an image name from the watch list.
```

Global options: `--json` makes `list` and `status` machine-readable;
`--no-color` (or the `NO_COLOR` environment variable) disables all colors.
See `awake aliases` for the shorthand forms.

## Installation

1. Extract `awake.exe` and `awake.daemon.exe` from this package into any
   folder. Both executables are statically linked and have no runtime
   dependencies.
2. Run `awake daemon on` (or simply `awake 1`) to start using the tool.
   The configuration file `awake.ini` is created next to the executables on
   first use; the first command also asks for the license.
3. Optional: run `awake daemon enable` to start the daemon automatically at
   every logon.

## Notes

- Keep-awake and screen keep-awake states live in the daemon's memory only;
  after a daemon restart they are inactive again (a running timed period
  expires with it).
- The daemon must not run elevated: an elevated shell cannot control a
  normal daemon afterwards. `AWAKE_ALLOW_ELEVATED=1` overrides this for
  automation environments.
- Daemon logging is enabled by default; disable it with `awake log off`.
- If you enabled autostart and later move the executables to another folder,
  `awake status` flags the stale entry and `awake daemon enable` in the new
  location fixes it.
- This is a pre-release; the behaviour and the command line interface may
  still change in incompatible ways before 1.0.
